t: Section 2710(b)(2) of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking subparagraph (B) and inserting the following:“(B) to any person with the informed, written consent (including through an electronic means using the Internet) of the consumer that—“(i) is in a form distinct and separate from any form setting forth other legal or financial obligations of the consumer;“(ii) at the election of the consumer—“(I) is given at the time the disclosure is sought; or“(II) is given in advance for a set period of time, not to exceed 2 years or until consent is withdrawn by the consumer, whichever is sooner; and“(iii) the video tape service provider has provided an opportunity, in a clear and conspicuous manner, for the consumer to withdraw on a case-by-case basis or to withdraw from ongoing disclosures, at the consumer’s election;”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the consumer's "consent" and "opportunity ... to withdraw" are a form of public input. That reading fails because the consent is given to a private video tape service provider about disclosing the consumer's own personal information, not to a federal agency before a federal decision. The section involves no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or newly granted right to sue the government.
fable.s: to any person with the informed, written consent (including through an electronic means using the Internet) of the consumer

qwen_block.w: This section establishes requirements for obtaining consumer consent for the disclosure of video tape service records. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a government decision. The interaction is between a private service provider and a consumer, not between the government and an outside party regarding a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: to any person with the informed, written consent (including through an electronic means using the Internet) of the consumer

opus.w: This amendment sets the rules for when a private video tape service provider may share a consumer's information, based on that consumer's consent. The consent and withdrawal steps sound procedural, but they happen entirely between private parties. No federal decision is involved, and there is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue a government decision. So this is not participation.
opus.s: the video tape service provider has provided an opportunity, in a clear and conspicuous manner, for the consumer to withdraw on a case-by-case basis or to withdraw from ongoing disclosures, at the consumer’s election
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is that "informed, written consent" and "an opportunity... for the consumer to withdraw" are outsiders taking part in a decision. That fails the definition's test. The consent and withdrawal happen between a private company (the video tape service provider) and its customer. No federal agency or official is making a decision, so no outsider is being brought into a federal decision. There is also no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body or right to sue a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes requirements for private video tape service providers to obtain consumer consent before disclosing records. It does not involve the federal government consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a federal decision. The interaction described is between a private entity and a consumer, which falls outside the definition of federal participation.
qwen_chat.s: to any person with the informed, written consent (including through an electronic means using the Internet) of the consumer
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring "informed, written consent" from a consumer constitutes participation because it involves an outside party (the consumer) agreeing to a process. However, this is a privacy/data protection provision regarding the disclosure of consumer records, not a mechanism for the consumer to consult with or influence a federal government decision. The interaction is between a private video tape service provider and a consumer, not the federal government and an outside party. The federal government is not making a decision here that requires consultation; it is setting rules for private entities.
